title: AI Interview System (overview)
text: The Adaptive Multimodal AI Interview & Candidate Assessment System is a 3-person team project and the final-month project of Jazib's PureLogics training, currently in progress. Candidates take a spoken interview with an AI interviewer, and recruiters review results in a dashboard. Jazib owns the real-time voice interview and the recruiter dashboard. His teammates build JD/CV eligibility matching and the interview question and assessment logic.

title: Voice pipeline
text: The voice interview uses real-time audio over LiveKit and a LiveKit Agents worker with custom speech-to-text, LLM and text-to-speech stages. The AI greets the candidate and asks the first question proactively. Barge-in (the candidate can interrupt the AI), silence detection, noise suppression and voice-triggered interview end all work end to end.

title: Speech-to-text and text-to-speech choices
text: Speech-to-text uses OpenAI Whisper (the small model) running locally on CPU, which is free and has no quota. Text-to-speech uses ElevenLabs as the primary voice, with a local fallback (Meta MMS-TTS) if the quota or rate limit fails. The team chose this cloud and local hybrid because the development laptop has no dedicated GPU.

title: Switching the interview to English
text: The team originally planned Roman Urdu support. With the supervisor's approval they moved the whole pipeline (speech-to-text, LLM and text-to-speech) to English, because speech recognition garbled English and Roman Urdu technical terms.

title: Data and persistence
text: Voice sessions are linked to real candidate application records. Completed interviews are saved as evaluated results in PostgreSQL, with Alembic migrations for candidates, job postings, applications and interview results. Saving is idempotent and only happens for eligible candidates with genuine evaluations.

title: Library Management System
text: The Library Management System for Quaid-e-Azam Library is a native Electron.js desktop app with a React.js frontend and a Node.js and Express backend, using MySQL through Sequelize ORM. It offers real-time automated book tracking, secure database architecture and native desktop integration. It was built from January 2026 to August 2026 and is completed. It was Jazib's final year project at the University of Education.
